correctness.rationale: The finite exchange kernel is the convolution of independent hypergeometric samples and has an exact affine mean and an O(n) variance bound. Stirling expansions yield a uniform one-step lattice Gaussian approximation once the preceding count is n/2+o_p(n); this holds uniformly after one step. The random centre has o(sqrt(n)) fluctuations because lambda tends to zero. The resulting fixed-time lattice Gaussian approximation and stationary hypergeometric local CLT produce the stated exact Gaussian total-variation profile, including the critical-window scaling. Standalone exact finite checker: 5325 assertions passed; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: In the inspected primary sources the half-exchange case has a vanishing three-step upper bound (Nestoridi and White, 2016) and only a two-to-C mixing-time bracket (Griffin et al., 2023). Alameda et al. (2022) assume a limiting swap fraction below one half. No inspected theorem implies the uniform fixed-time Gaussian profile or the n^{1-1/(2t)} transition scales; indexed-record searches did not identify an equivalent finding. General spectral formulas and unindexed literature remain residual priority risks.
residual_risks: Earlier dual-Hahn spectral formulas might be leveraged to derive the same statement by an unlocated argument, despite the inspected papers not stating or implying the profile directly.
Web and semantic-index searches are not exhaustive proof of historical originality; no independent mathematical or priority audit has been done.

value.rationale: The known critical half-swap analysis only guaranteed vanishing variation by three steps, while broader critical work gave bounded mixing. The new theorem establishes sharp two-step mixing, quantifies all fixed-time total-variation profiles, and isolates a natural nested family of n^{1-1/(2t)} exchange-size sensitivity windows. These are motivated finite-time distributions for interchange and shuffle processes, not a formal parameter renaming or an arbitrary finite experiment.
